channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Holding rates while watching inflation risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Bernd Weidensteiner expects the Federal Reserve to leave the policy rate at 3.50%–3.75% at the upcoming meeting, while debating potential hikes if inflation fails to ease.

item.title: Gold steadies after sharp drop as traders weigh Fed, Middle East risks
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) steadies on Friday after falling nearly 2% the previous day, as surging Oil prices fueled expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) may need to raise interest rates amid a worsening inflation outlook.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Oil surge offsets inflow support – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists highlight that the Indian Rupee (INR) stayed defensive as Brent Oil rose to $100, countering support from recent policy steps to attract capital inflows.

item.title: European Central Bank: September hike seen as highly likely – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists note that the European Central Bank (ECB) kept its deposit rate at 2.25%, while its communication continued to leave the door open to further tightening.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rebounds but upside remains limited as US Dollar stays supported
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5790 on Friday at the time of writing, up 0.27% on the day as the pair recovers from a one-and-a-half-week low, although bullish momentum remains limited by the underlying strength of the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: “Still see probability of rate hike higher than hold”: ECB’s Simkus expresses hawkish bias on rates
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member and head of Lithuania's central bank, Gediminas Simkus, said during European trading hours on Friday that the chances of an interest rate hike in the near term are higher than maintaining the status quo.

item.title: US S&P Global PMI expected to show steady business growth in July
item.description: S&P Global will release the July flash Purchasing Managers' Indices (PMIs) for the United States (US) on Friday. These surveys of top private-sector executives are seen as an early indicator of the country’s economic health.

item.title: Turkish Lira: Tight CBRT funding offers marginal support – Commerzbank
item.description: According to Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose, the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (CBRT) kept its one-week repo rate at 37.0% and maintained the corridor at 35.5%-40.0%. With the repo window still closed, effective funding remains near 40%, which Ghose views as Lira-supportive.

item.title: Euro holds steady vs British Pound after stronger Eurozone, UK data
item.description: EUR/GBP trades around 0.8550 at the time of writing on Friday, remaining broadly stable despite a series of stronger-than-expected economic releases from the Eurozone and the United Kingdom (UK).

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $58.40 per troy ounce, up 1.98% from the $57.27 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: Indian Rupee holds early gains amid renewed RBI intervention rumours
item.description: The Indian Rupee gains strongly after a flat opening against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday. The USD/INR pair declines to near 96.50 as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has intervened again to support the Indian Rupee.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed expectations keep upside in focus – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes the US Dollar (USD) is supported as higher energy prices fuel expectations of further central bank tightening, with markets pricing more hikes from the European Central Bank (ECB) and Bank of England (BoE).

item.title: British Pound retreats from 1.3340 as bright UK data fails to offset risk aversion
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) remains depressed near three-week lows against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, with upside attempts capped below 1.3340, and on track for a 1% weekly decline.

item.title: Japanese Yen remains pinned near 40-year low as Fed-BoJ rate gap keeps carry trade active
item.description: The USD/JPY pair edges lower on Friday as bulls turn cautious in anticipation of a potential government intervention to prop up the Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: Gold climbs above $4,050 on retreating USD; upside seems limited amid Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) builds on its modest intraday bounce and climbs back above the $4,050 level, hitting a fresh daily high during the first half of the European session on Friday amid a modest US Dollar (USD) pullback.

item.title: Euro: Rate support seen fading gradually against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny says the ECB’s latest communication supports a likely September rate hike, now almost fully priced, but warns that Euro support may fade as energy costs rise.

item.title: UK S&P Global Services PMI returns to growth in July, arrives at 51.8
item.description: According to preliminary data, the United Kingdom (UK) S&P Global Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) arrives above 50.0 in July, a figure that separates expansion from contraction, after declining in June.

item.title: South African Rand: SARB surprise weighs against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur says the South African Reserve Bank’s (SARB) decision to keep its policy rate unchanged at 7% came as a negative surprise, particularly after June inflation rose and Brent crude moved above USD 100 per barrel.

item.title: Euro remains capped below 1.1400 despite bright Eurozone preliminary PMIs
item.description: The Euro (EUR) ticks up against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday but remains capped below 1.1400, and dangerously close to the year-to-date low, at 1.1324.

item.title: Gold: Oil-led inflation fears cap recovery – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey report that Gold has come under pressure as higher Oil prices stoke inflation concerns and push yields and the US Dollar higher.

item.title: United States Dollar Index Price Forecast: Pullbacks could be bought into near 101.00
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, drifts lower during the early European session on Friday and erodes a part of the previous day's strong gains back closer to the monthly high.

item.title: Eurozone flash Manufacturing PMI rises surprisingly faster-than-estimates to 52.0
item.description: Preliminary HCOB Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) in the oldest continent expands at a faster pace to 52.0 in July from June’s figure of 51.4. The manufacturing activity was anticipated to expand but at a moderate pace to 51.3.

item.title: Dow Jones futures bounce back as oil cools, though geopolitical risks persist
item.description: Dow Jones futures gain 0.35% to trade around 52,070 during European trading hours on Friday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq 100 futures advance 0.21% and 0.08%, trading near 7,460 and 28,650, respectively.

item.title: Silver Price Forecasts: XAG/USD edges up above $58.00 as the US Dollar trims gains
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) edges up on Friday's early European trading session, returning to levels above $58.00 as the US Dollar trims some gains.

item.title: Brent: War premium drives triple-digit prices – UOB
item.description: UOB Global Economics & Markets Research highlights that escalating US-Iran tensions and Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping have driven Brent crude above US$100 for the first time since May, with Asia trading near US$101.

item.title: Germany’s flash Manufacturing PMI unexpectedly rises strongly to 52.2 vs. 50.1 estimates
item.description: German flash HCOB Composite PMI returns to the expansion trajectory in July after declining in June. Preliminary figures show that the overall business activity expanded to 51.2. The Composite PMI was seen arriving at 49.8 from 49.5 in June.

item.title: Forex Today: New wave of US tariffs, deepening Middle East conflict keep markets on edge
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Friday, July 24:

item.title: Equities: Oil shock and tech earnings hit equities – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists highlight that the S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell sharply as surging Oil prices and stagflation fears weighed on risk assets. Weak post‑earnings reactions in Tesla and Alphabet dragged the Mag 7 index to its biggest daily loss since 2025.

item.title: Russian Ruble: CBR seen holding rate despite pressure to cut – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose expects Russia’s central bank to keep its key rate at 14.25%, despite political and economic pressure for a cut. Surging inflation expectations, higher Oil and commodity prices, and accelerating Consumer Price Index (CPI) argue against easing.

item.title: British Pound steadies against Japanese Yen following outperformance in UK Retail Sales
item.description: GBP/JPY remains calm after six days of losses, trading around 218.20 during the early European hours on Friday. The currency cross holds its ground as the British Pound (GBP) receives support from the release of stronger-than-expected UK Retail Sales data.
